chunks: 4188 - And in the narration of Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
He was asked about a man who slaughters and then forgets to mention the name of Allah: may his slaughtered animal be eaten?
He said: "Yes, if he is not suspected, and he performs slaughter well from before that, and he does not sever the spinal cord nor break the neck until the slaughtered animal has cooled."

key_terms.تَبْرُدَ الذَّبِيحَةُ: the slaughtered animal becomes cool, i.e. its motion ceases
key_terms.لَا يُتَّهَمُ: he is not regarded with suspicion or accused of unreliability
key_terms.يَذْبَحُ: he slaughters an animal in the legal sense
key_terms.يَنْخَعُ: he severs the spinal cord in slaughter
key_terms.يُحْسِنُ الذَّبْحَ: he performs slaughter properly and correctly
key_terms.يُسَمِّيَ: to mention the name of Allah at the time of slaughter

ai.seo_question: Can meat be eaten if the slaughterer forgot to say the name of Allah during slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on the permissibility of an animal slaughtered by someone who forgot to mention the name of Allah. The ruling is conditioned by the slaughterer being trustworthy, known to slaughter properly, and avoiding prohibited excesses such as severing the spinal cord or breaking the neck before the animal has fully stilled.
